source_text: Scripturarum sane testimonia quaedam latius exposui, quaedam brevius; quia me plene id secuturo opere facturum spopondi. Nihil itaque ibi de omnibus Augustini argumentis et propositionibus non explosum remansit, nihil a me impletum est aliter quam promissum; multa in inventis eius falsa, multa stolida, sacrilega multa convici.
pass_a_gloss: Some testimonies of the Scriptures I explained more widely, some more briefly; because I pledged that I would do it fully in the work that would follow. Nothing therefore there of all Augustine's arguments and propositions remained unexploded, nothing was fulfilled by me otherwise than promised; many false things, many stupid things, many sacrilegious things I convicted in his inventions.
pass_b_english: I explained some scriptural testimonies at greater length and others more briefly, because I promised to handle them fully in the work that would follow. Thus none of Augustine's arguments and propositions there remained without refutation, and I carried out nothing differently from what I had promised. I exposed many falsehoods, many absurdities, and many sacrileges in his inventions.

choices.why: Julian's sacred writings; keep Scripture, not 'Bible' as a later book-name.
Proof-text, especially Rom 5:12 in this book; keep 'testimony' not 'verse'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
